title: config-driven-retry-profiles-and-unified-iterable-apis-across-sdks
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces config-driven retry profiles and a unified iterable/pull-stream consumer surface across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Backwards-compatible adapter hooks provided; SDK minor version bumps. No breaking API changes expected.
body:
Context: Teams report inconsistent retry behavior across SDKs and awkward ergonomics when consuming streaming responses (different iterator/callback patterns per language). This PR unifies the developer experience by introducing: 1) a config-driven retry profile abstraction (gentlebackoff/adaptive/strict) that is serializable and can be passed to SDK constructors; 2) a consistent iterable/pull-stream surface for streaming responses in Python, TypeScript, and Go; 3) lightweight adapter layers for existing callbacks to maintain backwards compatibility; 4) a credential lease hook to smooth token rotation during long-lived streams.

Motivation: reduce cognitive load for cross-platform teams, enable server-side recommendations (Optimize) to suggest retry profiles, and fix edge cases where reauth during stream reconnects caused duplicate events or lost messages.

Design summary: - Retry profiles are plain objects with named profiles (gentlebackoff, balanced, aggressive) and pluggable backoff strategies. SDKs expose a `RetryProfile` config and a `retry_profile` field in client constructors. - Streaming surface: introduce `iter_stream()` in Python (async iterator + sync iterator fallback), `streamIterable()` in TypeScript (AsyncIterable + friendly for for-await), and `StreamIterator` in Go that supports Pause/Resume and Idempotent Resume tokens. - Auth lease hook: credential providers can optionally implement `lease()` returning a short-lived token window; the runtime will prefetch and swap tokens gracefully while preserving a per-stream handshake. - Backwards compatibility: existing `.stream()` methods are shims that call into the new iterables; we provide migration docs and a small compatibility adapter shipped in each SDK package.

Implementation notes: changes touch SDK surface layers only, with minimal runtime changes in the core redwood server to honor the named retry profiles for hosted routes.

Tests: added cross-sdk integration tests that exercise reconnect during token rotation, retry profile effect on transient 5xxs, and stream resume semantics.

Checklist: - [x] TypeScript impl and tests - [x] Python impl and tests - [x] Go impl and tests - [x] Auth lease hook integrated - [x] Migration docs and examples - [x] CI green - [x] Release notes Draft

Commits summary: short, focused commits each per language and docs.

Files changed (high level): - redwood-sdk-typescript/src/stream/iterable.ts (new unified iterable implementation) - redwood-sdk-python/redwood/stream/iterable.py (new async/sync iterator) - redwood-sdk-go/stream/iterator.go (pause/resume tokens) - shared-specs/retry-profiles.yaml (canonical profiles) - docs/sdk/migration/retry-profiles.md - examples/streaming/typed-iterables/* - tests/integration/stream-resume-reauth.test.ts - tests/integration/stream-resume-reauth_test.py - tests/integration/stream_resume_reauth_test.go

Review notes and discussion: - Ethan: requested clearer guarantees for ordering during token swap — added a short section in the body and tests that validate ordering is preserved for per-request monotonic sequence ids. - Sofia: asked to ensure the new retry config can be passed via environment/JSON for Redwood Optimize to suggest overrides — implemented parsing of env var REDWOOD_RETRY_PROFILE and added docs. - Diego: requested smaller surface area for Go ergonomics — we trimmed the iterator API to fewer exported methods and provided a small helper to expose Pause/Resume semantics. CI: initially flaked on e2e streaming; re-run fixed intermittent infra flakiness and all checks passed.

Merge plan: squash-merge into main after approvals; post-merge we will publish SDK minor releases: python 1.12.0, typescript 2.4.0, go v1.9.0 and update CDN docs.

Rollout: behind feature flag on the hosted API to opt-in retry-profile forwarding; SDKs default to "balanced" to keep behavior steady.

Migration guidance: short adapter example in migration doc showing how to convert old stream callback usage to the new async iterator (TS) or sync iterator (Python).
